Through: Mr  wi  Ms  pr  CORAM:
 HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE MANOJ KUMAR OHRI  ORDER % 06.11.2025 CRL.M.(BAIL) 895/2024 (suspension of sentence)
1. The present application has been filed seeking suspension of sentence during the pendency of the appeal.
2.

By way of appeal, the appellant seeks to assail the judgement of conviction dated 23.12.2022 and order on sentence dated 05.04.2023 passed by learned ASJ-05/(POCSO), North District, Rohini Courts, Delhi vide which he has been directed to undergo RI for a period of 7 years for the offence punishable under Section 376 IPC and fine of Rs.1,000/-, in default thereof to undergo SI for 15 days.

entities.text: ASJ-05/(POCSO), North District, Rohini Courts, Delhi
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: He was further sentenced to undergo rigorous imprisonment for 6 months for the offence punishable under section 9 of Prohibition of Child Marriage Act.

The benefit of Section 428 Cr.P.C.
has also been provided to the appellant and all the sentences have been directed to run concurrently.
This is a digitally signed order.

The Order is downloaded from the DHC Server on 06/11/2025 at 22:50:03 3.

Learned counsel appearing for the appellant/applicant submits that the appellant/applicant was about 22 years of age and believing the victim to be more than 18 years of age, performed the marriage with her in a temple.

He further states that though the prosecution has later alleged the Arun vs State Nct Of Delhi on 6 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/82771455/
1 victim to be of 12 years of age, however failed to prove the same.

sentences.text: Lastly, it is stated that out of the total sentence of 7 years awarded to the appellant, he has already undergone more than half of his sentence.

In this regard, he has placed reliance on the decisions in Saudan Singh vs. The State of Uttar Pradesh reported as 2021 SCC OnLine SC 3259 and Sonadhar vs. The State of Chhattisgarh reported as 2021 SCC OnLine SC 3182.
4.

sentences.text: The application is opposed by learned APP appearing for the State duly assisted by learned counsel appearing for the victim to submit that the marriage performed by the appellant is no marriage in the eyes of law and that the victim was a minor at the relevant time.
5. I have heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record placed before me.
6. As per the interaction form and the nominal roll on record, it is noted that the appellant has undergone more than half his sentence.

7. The contentions made on behalf of appellant would require detailed consideration at the time of final hearing however, having gone through the testimony of victim and other records and keeping in view of the above and the decision in Saudan Singh vs. The State of Uttar Pradesh reported as 2021 SCC OnLine SC 3259 and Sonadhar vs. The State of Chhattisgarh reported as 2021 SCC OnLine SC 3182 and the further fact that the hearing of the appeal will take some time, the sentence of the appellant/applicant is suspended during the pendency of the appeal on his furnishing of a personal This is a digitally signed order.

(i) In case of change of residential address, the appellant shall promptly inform the same to the concerned Investigating Officer as well as to this Court.
( ii) The appellant shall regularly appear before the Court as and when the appeal is taken up for hearing.
(iii) The appellant will not get in touch directly or indirectly with the victim.
(iv) The appellant shall also provider his contact number to the IO and shall remain available on that number.
8. With the above directions, the application is disposed of.
9. A copy of this order be communicated electronically forthwith to the concerned Jail Superintendent for information and necessary compliance.
